To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rate of hot pixel defect development in a camera is a function of pixel size, sensor size, and ISO.
the defect rate of a sensor is proportional to its area and to the square of its pixel size, while it increases with the gain (ISO).

the defect rate of hot pixel defects is linear with sensor area, and the power law of the defect density is proportional to the pixel area and the ISO, with different exponents for CCD and APS (CMOS).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an analytical tool to predict the rate of development of hot pixel defects over time for any given camera, as well as the expected number of hot pixels for any given image.
the statistical analysis of the development of hot pixel defects in image sensors, and their dependence on sensor design parameters.
understanding the defect development of in-field hot pixel defects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rate at which hot pixel defects accumulate in the field is proportional to the sensor size, to the pixel size, and to the square root of ISO.
hot pixel defects are proportional to the sensor size to the power -1, and to the ISO to the 0.6 power.
defect density is proportional to pixel size to the negative power of 2.5 to 3.1 and ISO to the power between 0.5 and 0.7.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the defect density of hot pixel defects is proportional to the pixel area to the power of ~3.5, and to the gain to the power of about 0.5, and that this defect density scales with sensor area.
the defect density is inversely proportional to the pixel area to the power of ~3 and to the ISO to the ~0.6.
the defect rate is proportional to the square of the pixel size and inversely proportional to the ISO.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the defect development rate is not only dependent on the technology, and on sensor size, but also on the gain (or ISO).
the defect rate for any given pixel size and ISO can be predicted by the formulae presented in this work.
defect rates can be estimated for a given camera, based on sensor parameters and technology, allowing us to predict the number of defects that will be present at a given time.
